title: Seed Priming with Plant Growth Regulators Improves Physiological and Biochemical Attributes of Pea and Plantago Seedlings Grown Under Artificial Magnetism
content: Seed-priming is an essential phenomenon of today’s agricultural practices which is widely being utilized for better seed stand development of plants. Priming of seeds with essential plant growth regulators (PGRs) such as; hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), salicylic acid (SA), ascorbic acid (AsA), gibberellic acid (GA3), potassium nitrate (KNO3) including H2O priming treatment for 12 hours is highly beneficial to promote plant effectiveness under different environmental circumstances including artificial magnetism (north, south and north/south). The present study was carried out during September 2022 in Department of Botany, University of Balochistan, Quetta to investigate the physiological and biochemical attributes of two important plant species; Plantago ovata Forrsk. (Plantago) and Pisum sativum (pea) under artificial magnetism. Design of experiment was completely randomized design (CRD) comprising three replications. Results of different parameters portrayed that priming of seeds with essential PGRs is a novel technique to enhance plant growth and development. The overall accumulation of secondary metabolites such as; anthocyanin, soluble sugars and phenolics, tannins contents in pea plants showed significant (p < 0.05) variations except shoot tannin which showed non-significant (p > 0.05) results under artificial magnetic treatments in combination with supplementation of SA, KNO3, AsA and GA3 primed seeds as compared to plantago seedlings. Moreover, the status of nutrients, i.e., potassium in both shoots showed non-significant results by accumulating higher contents as compared to root, while in both plants seedlings, manganese content showed significant differences in root and shoot under priming. Astonishingly, the oxidative damage parameters (hydrogen peroxide and malondialdehyde) decreased by illustrating non-significant interactions among root and shoot. In overall study, pea seedlings performed very well under artificial magnetism by the pre-soaking of seeds with PGRs as compared to plantago seedlings. Therefore, the present study highly encourages the phenomenon of PGRs seed-priming along with artificial magnetic treatment for the better growth and development of plants seedlings and more importantly, pea and plantago.
